sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ragallach, also written Raghallach, is an Irish hero. Tis said Ragallach governed Connacht, the western Irish province, during the seventh century. Some records give historical evidence for his rule, though the rich tales about him stay partly legend. Greedy for power, Ragallach arranged the killing of his nephew, his one rival for the throne, who had come guarded but was shamed into leaving his guards behind, letting the king kill him easily. For this the druids foretold that Ragallach would die by his own children. Seeking to escape the prophecy, he commanded that every one of his children be put to death. His queen Murieann concealed their unnamed daughter in the forest, where a poor woman brought her up. She grew into a famous beauty, and the king, not knowing she was his child, demanded she be brought to him. Insulted, Murieann left the court. In protest holy men went without food, and on the following Beltane eve the king fell under magic power.

okr.objective: Ragallach is a greedy Connacht king undone by his own cruelty.
